n60d6caace76.s: Which type of hydroelectric plant uses the natural flow of a river with little or no storage?
n60d6caace76.x: A run-of-the-river plant uses the natural flow with little or no storage; a storage plant uses a dam to regulate output.

n7566dfc54d2.s: About what share of India's hydroelectric potential of over 145 GW has been developed?
n7566dfc54d2.x: Only about 36% of India's hydro potential of over 145 GW has been developed.

nc9d6749d71c.s: Under Revised SHAKTI, coal at the notified price is given under:
nc9d6749d71c.x: Window-I gives coal at the notified price; Window-II involves bidding at a premium.

nf1aecc8fdcf.s: Batteries, pumped storage, cyclical gas operation and hydro optimisation are measures of:
o: Flexible operation of the power system
nf1aecc8fdcf.x: These four are the measures for flexible operation of the power system alongside coal plants.

ndffaece6494.s: Under the Swarna Andhra Vision, Andhra Pradesh targets a renewable-energy share of more than ____ by 2047.
ndffaece6494.x: AP's RE share is about 30% now and the target is more than 75% by 2047 under the Swarna Andhra Vision.

nc11e85a00cb.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Homi Bhabha's three-stage nuclear programme?
o: It aims at self-reliance through a closed fuel cycle
It seeks to overcome India's scarcity of uranium
It makes use of India's abundant thorium
It was designed to use abundant uranium in place of scarce thorium
nc11e85a00cb.x: The programme uses abundant thorium to overcome scarce uranium, not the other way round.

n35fbfddaa97.s:
Consider the following statements about India's nuclear power:
1. NPCIL operates 25 reactors with an operating capacity of 8,880 MW.
2. India's nuclear capacity target is 22.38 GW by 2031-32.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n35fbfddaa97.x: Both figures are correct: 25 reactors with 8,880 MW, and a target of 22.38 GW by 2031-32.

n5e3ff12621e.s: In a nuclear reactor, the component that slows down neutrons is the:
n5e3ff12621e.x: The moderator slows neutrons; the coolant carries heat and control rods absorb neutrons.

nf754f7d4c34.s:
Arrange the following research reactors in ascending order of capacity:
1. Dhruva
2. KAMINI
3. CIRUS
nf754f7d4c34.x: KAMINI is 30 kW, CIRUS 40 MW and Dhruva, India's largest research reactor, 100 MW.

n627feccf433.s: Which Nuclear Security Summit–year pair is correctly matched?
n627feccf433.x: The summits were Washington 2010, Seoul 2012, The Hague 2014 and Washington 2016, the last.

n918a33d22fd.s:
Consider the following statements about the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB):
1. It was set up on 15 November 1983 by an executive order under the Atomic Energy Act, 1962.
2. It got statutory status when the Nuclear Safety Regulatory Authority Bill was enacted.
3. It got statutory status under the SHANTI Act, 2025.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
n918a33d22fd.x: The AERB was created by executive order in 1983; the NSRA Bill was never enacted and statutory status came with the SHANTI Act, 2025.

new.s: The Machkund hydroelectric project is a joint project of Andhra Pradesh and:
new.x: Machkund (114.75 MW) is an AP-Odisha joint project.

new.s: The Srisailam Right Bank hydro station, which belongs to Andhra Pradesh, has a capacity of:
new.x: Srisailam Right Bank (770 MW) is AP's; the 900 MW Left Bank is Telangana's.

new.s: The Lower Sileru hydroelectric project has an installed capacity of:
new.x: Lower Sileru has 4 x 115 = 460 MW; 240 MW is Upper Sileru hydro.

new.s: The largest pumped-storage project in Andhra Pradesh, Upper Sileru PSP, has a capacity of:
new.x: Upper Sileru PSP is 1,350 MW (9 x 150); 240 MW is the Upper Sileru hydro station and 1,680 MW is Pinnapuram.

new.s: The AP Pumped Storage Promotion Policy 2022 identified 29 locations with a total potential of:
new.x: The 2022 policy lists 29 locations with 33,240 MW.

new.s: The 1,000 MW Tehri pumped-storage plant, fully commissioned on 12 April 2026, is in:
new.x: Tehri PSP (4 x 250 MW) is in Uttarakhand.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Sharavathi PSP in Karnataka is 2,000 MW; Tehri PSP is 1,000 MW and Pinnapuram is in Kurnool.

new.s: Large hydro projects (above 25 MW) were declared renewable energy in:
new.x: Large hydro was declared renewable in March 2019, though it stays under the Ministry of Power.

new.s: In 1989, small hydro projects up to what capacity were moved to the MNRE?
new.x: Small hydro up to 3 MW moved to MNRE in 1989; the ceiling was raised to 25 MW in November 1999.

new.s: India has 6,628 specified large dams. Which State has the most of them?
new.x: Maharashtra has the most specified dams, followed by Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about hydro data of India:
1. India ranks 3rd in the world in large dams.
2. Small-hydro potential is 21,133 MW at 6,628 sites.
3. Installed large hydro capacity is about 51.96 GW.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: India is 3rd in large dams and has 51.96 GW of large hydro; small-hydro potential is at 7,133 sites, while 6,628 is the number of specified dams.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about large dams?
o: Himalayan dams carry a seismic risk
About 18.5 million people were affected by displacement in 1950-90
new.x: Dams block fish migration; they do not improve it.

new.s: The movement against the Tehri dam on the Bhagirathi was led by:
new.x: Sunderlal Bahuguna led the anti-Tehri movement; Medha Patkar led the Narmada Bachao Andolan.

new.s: The Narmada Bachao Andolan was mainly directed against which project?
new.x: The Narmada Bachao Andolan, led by Medha Patkar, opposed the Sardar Sarovar project.

new.s: Under the Dam Safety Act 2021, which body frames policy and standards?
new.x: The NCDS frames policy and standards; the NDSA is the regulator that implements policy.

new.s: The World Commission on Dams brought out its report 'Dams and Development' in:
new.x: The WCD, set up in 1998 by the World Bank and IUCN, published 'Dams and Development' in 2000.

new.s: The Nathpa Jhakri hydroelectric project (1,500 MW) is on which river?
new.x: Nathpa Jhakri in Himachal Pradesh is on the Satluj.

new.s: The Koyna hydroelectric project of 1,960 MW is in:
new.x: Koyna (1,960 MW) is on the Koyna river in Maharashtra.

new.s: The Tehri hydro project in Uttarakhand is built on which river?
new.x: Tehri is on the Bhagirathi in Uttarakhand.

new.s: Which is India's largest thermal power plant?
new.x: Vindhyachal (4,760 MW, NTPC) in Singrauli, MP, is the largest; Mundra is 4,620 MW.

new.s: Which thermal plant–State pair is correctly matched?
new.x: Talcher (Kaniha) is in Odisha; Tiroda is in Maharashtra, Mundra in Gujarat and Vindhyachal in MP.

new.s: The Mundra UMPP was developed by:
new.x: Mundra UMPP is Tata Power's; the other Mundra plant (4,620 MW) is Adani's.

new.s: The Rayalaseema Thermal Power Plant (1,650 MW) is located at:
new.x: RTPP is at Muddanur in Kadapa; Dr NTTPS is at Ibrahimpatnam.

new.s: The Simhadri thermal power station at Visakhapatnam belongs to:
new.x: Simhadri in Visakhapatnam is an NTPC plant.

new.s: Which State ranks first in installed thermal power capacity (UPPSC 2008)?
new.x: The ranking is Maharashtra, Gujarat, West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: Under the SAMARTH mission (2021), coal power plants must co-fire what share of biomass?
new.x: The SAMARTH mission mandates 5% biomass co-firing.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about coal power plants:
1. They are the largest emitters of CO2.
2. They emit PM2.5.
3. They use little water.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Coal plants are the largest CO2 source and emit PM2.5; they use heavy amounts of water.

new.s: U-235 makes up about what share of natural uranium?
new.x: Fissile U-235 is only 0.72% of natural uranium; fertile U-238 is 99.28%.

new.s: Light water reactors need uranium enriched to about ____ U-235.
new.x: LWRs need 3–5% U-235, above the natural 0.72%.

new.s: U-238 is a fertile isotope. Into which fissile material is it converted?
new.x: U-238 absorbs a neutron and becomes fissile Pu-239; Th-232 becomes U-233.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about nuclear isotopes?
new.x: U-238 is fertile, not fissile; the fissile fuel bred from it is Pu-239.

new.s: The minimum mass of fissile material that can sustain a chain reaction is called:
new.x: Critical mass is the minimum fissile mass for a chain reaction; criticality is the self-sustaining state itself.

new.s: The bomb 'Little Boy' dropped on Hiroshima used which fissile material?
new.x: Little Boy (Hiroshima) used U-235; Fat Man (Nagasaki) used Pu-239.

new.s: Who is called the 'father of the hydrogen bomb'?
new.x: Edward Teller is the father of the hydrogen bomb; Otto Hahn gave the fission principle.

new.s: Radioactivity was discovered by Henri Becquerel in:
new.x: Becquerel discovered radioactivity in 1896.

new.s: The natural thorium decay series starts with Th-232 and ends in:
new.x: The thorium series runs Th-232 to Pb-208; the uranium series ends in Pb-206, and the neptunium series is artificial.

new.s: Gamma radiation is stopped by:
new.x: Gamma rays need lead or concrete; alpha is stopped by paper and beta by a few mm of aluminium.

new.s: Which reactor type has no moderator and uses liquid sodium as coolant?
new.x: The FBR uses fast neutrons, so it needs no moderator; it is cooled by liquid sodium.

new.s: Which reactor type–Indian example pair is correctly matched?
new.x: Tarapur has BWRs; Kudankulam has PWR/VVER units and the FBR is at Kalpakkam.

new.s: Who is known as the 'Father of the Indian nuclear programme'?
new.x: Homi J. Bhabha planned the three-stage programme in the 1950s and is its father.

new.s: Stage II of India's three-stage nuclear programme uses which fuel?
new.x: Stage II FBRs burn MOX of Pu-239 and U-238; Stage I uses natural uranium and Stage III thorium with U-233.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a hurdle to reaching Stage III of the nuclear programme?
new.x: India has abundant thorium; the hurdles are thin fissile inventory, long builds and protests.

new.s: The Fast Breeder Test Reactor (FBTR) at Kalpakkam first attained criticality in:
new.x: The FBTR, based on the French Rapsodie design, went critical on 18 October 1985.

new.s: India's largest research reactor is:
new.x: Dhruva (100 MW) at Trombay is the largest; APSARA was the first.

new.s: The world's only U-233-fuelled reactor, KAMINI, is located at:
new.x: KAMINI (30 kW) is at IGCAR, Kalpakkam.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about monazite?
o: It is the principal ore of thorium
It contains rare earths such as lanthanum and cerium
Only IREL-type government bodies may process and export it
It occurs along the entire Indian coast
new.x: Monazite occurs in beach sands of Kerala, TN, Odisha, AP and others, not along the entire coast.

new.s: India holds about what share of the world's uranium?
new.x: India has about 2% of world uranium against about 25% of thorium.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a member of ITER?
new.x: ITER is the EU plus India, China, Japan, South Korea, Russia and USA; Canada is not a member.

new.s: Which component of ITER does India supply?
new.x: India, a member since 2005, supplies the cryostat.

new.s: Aditya, India's first tokamak, belongs to:
new.x: Aditya and SST-1 are at IPR Gandhinagar, not BARC.

new.s: Which nuclear body–seat pair is correctly matched?
new.x: AMD (atomic minerals exploration) and NFC are at Hyderabad; UCIL is at Jaduguda and IGCAR at Kalpakkam.

new.s: The Indira Gandhi Centre for Atomic Research (IGCAR) was established in:
new.x: IGCAR at Kalpakkam was set up in 1971 for FBR technology.

new.s: The Nuclear Energy Mission (Budget 2025-26) earmarks how much for Small Modular Reactors?
new.x: The Mission sets ₹20,000 crore for SMRs and a target of 100 GW by 2047.

new.s: The SHANTI Act 2025 repealed the CLNDA 2010 and which other law?
new.x: SHANTI repealed the Atomic Energy Act 1962 and CLNDA 2010, not the 1948 Act.

new.s: The Gorakhpur (GHAVP) nuclear power project is located in:
new.x: Gorakhpur NPP is in Haryana; Narora is the plant in Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: The Narora atomic power station is in which State?
new.x: Narora (2 x 220 MW PHWR, Seismic Zone IV) is in Uttar Pradesh.

new.s: Which nuclear power station is located near the Kali river in Uttara Kannada?
new.x: Kaiga (4 units, 880 MW) in Karnataka is near the Kali river.

new.s: The standard sizes of India's PHWR units have grown in which order?
new.x: PHWR unit sizes went 220 → 540 → 700 MW, all indigenised.

new.s: Which is the largest planned nuclear power project in India?
new.x: Jaitapur (6 EPRs, 9,900 MW) is the largest planned; Kudankulam (2,000 MW) is the largest operating.

new.s: Chutka 1-2, among the fleet-mode 700 MW PHWRs, is in:
new.x: Chutka is in Madhya Pradesh; Mahi Banswara is in Rajasthan and Kaiga 5-6 in Karnataka.

new.s: Nuclear power's share of India's installed power capacity is about:
new.x: Nuclear is 1.62% of installed capacity but about 3.1% of generation.

new.s: Which country was the top nuclear-power generator in 2024?
new.x: The USA led, followed by China, France, Russia and South Korea; France gets the largest share of its electricity from nuclear.

new.s: In FY2024-25, India's nuclear generation set a record of:
new.x: Generation reached 56.681 BU, the first time above 50 BU.

new.s: All heavy water plants in India function under the Heavy Water Board, located at:
new.x: The Heavy Water Board, under DAE, is at Trombay, Mumbai.

new.s: The Kudankulam plant's two running units are of which reactor type?
new.x: Kudankulam runs 2 x VVER-1000 (Russia); Jaitapur is to have EPRs and Kovvada AP1000s.

new.s: What is the present status of the Kovvada nuclear power project?
new.x: Kovvada is at the pre-construction stage; Westinghouse had yet to submit its techno-commercial offer (Nov 2024).

new.s: How many AP1000 reactors are proposed at Kovvada?
new.x: Kovvada is to have six AP1000 PWRs by Westinghouse, USA.

new.s: The NSG waiver of September 2008 ended how many years of India's exclusion from nuclear trade?
new.x: The 2008 waiver ended 34 years of exclusion and allowed civil nuclear trade.

new.s: India's civil nuclear agreement with Australia was signed in:
new.x: The India–Australia deal was signed in 2014 and came into force in 2015.

new.s: India signed the India-Specific Safeguards Agreement with the IAEA on:
new.x: The India-Specific Safeguards Agreement was signed on 2 February 2009.

new.s: India's application for NSG membership has been blocked mainly by:
new.x: China blocks India's entry, citing India's absence from the NPT; Australia supports it.

new.s: Which of these nuclear treaties has India signed?
new.x: India signed the PTBT (1963); it has not signed the NPT, CTBT or TPNW.

new.s: Under the CLNDA 2010, operator liability was capped at:
new.x: CLNDA capped no-fault operator liability at ₹1,500 crore, with the Centre paying beyond it.

new.s: Which section of the CLNDA 2010 gave the operator a right of recourse against suppliers?
new.x: Section 17(b) gave recourse against suppliers; Section 46 kept other civil laws open.

new.s: The exclusion zone around an Indian nuclear reactor, with no public habitation, has a radius of about:
new.x: The exclusion zone is 1–1.5 km (APPSC 2022 key: 1 km); 16 km is the Emergency Planning Zone.

new.s: The Three Mile Island accident (1979) took place in:
new.x: Three Mile Island was in Pennsylvania, USA, in 1979.

new.s: On the INES scale, the Three Mile Island accident was rated:
new.x: Three Mile Island was level 5; only Chernobyl and Fukushima are level 7.

new.s: At the 2010 Nuclear Security Summit, India announced the GCNEP, now located at:
new.x: India announced the Global Centre for Nuclear Energy Partnership in 2010; it is at Bahadurgarh.
